title: Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy has directly imaged electronic crystals in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, and magnetotransport measurements suggest that superconductivity and charge-density-wave order emerge from a common spin-valley-polarized ferromagnetic metal at nearby carrier densities. Motivated by these observations, we ask whether collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate pairing in this setting. We address this question by studying the Cooper problem for two electrons in the first conduction band of the Wigner crystal. Unlike conventional phonon-mediated pairing, the collective mode (boson) energies and single-particle (fermion) dispersion are comparable scales controlled by the electron density, leaving no small parameter for an adiabatic expansion. Moreover, because the magnetic Wigner crystal is not time-reversal invariant, the usual Cooper logarithmic divergence in the pairing susceptibility is absent, so the attraction must exceed a finite threshold for pairing to occur. These unusual features motivate a numerical experiment to see whether the crystal's own vibrations can bind electrons. We obtain the crystalline ground state and its collective mode spectrum within Hartree--Fock and time-dependent Hartree--Fock approximation, and derive the electron--phonon Hamiltonian using the quasiboson approximation. Solving the resulting two-electron problem, we find that phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, with chiral $p$-wave pairing as the leading instability. Within these approximations, we show that collective modes of a Wigner crystal can indeed favor chiral pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry. Our results provide an encouraging starting point for developing a full many-body theory to study electronic crystallization and superconductivity.
summary: This theoretical work explores superconductivity in a magnetic Wigner crystal realized in graphene. By modeling the electron-phonon interaction, the authors demonstrate that the crystal's own vibrations can induce a pairing attraction strong enough to cause superconductivity. The resulting superconducting state is predicted to exhibit chiral p-wave pairing, providing a theoretical pathway for understanding electronic crystallization and pairing in correlated 2D materials.
main_problem: The study investigates whether collective vibrational modes (phonons) within a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate an attractive interaction strong enough to induce electron pairing (Cooper instability).
main_result: The calculations show that the phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, leading to the prediction of chiral p-wave pairing as the leading superconducting instability.
method: The authors employed a combination of Hartree-Fock and time-dependent Hartree-Fock approximations to derive an effective fermion-boson Hamiltonian, which was then solved using the quasiboson approximation for the two-electron Cooper problem.
model_or_system: The system is a magnetic Wigner crystal formed by electrons in the first conduction band of rhombohedral hexalayer graphene. The model treats the interaction via coupling to the crystal's collective bosonic excitations (phonons and plasmons).
key_observables: Pairing susceptibility, binding energy ($E_b$), and the momentum-space phase texture ($\chi_0(k)$) which exhibits a winding consistent with chiral p-wave pairing.
important_parameters: Electron density ($n = 0.8 	imes 10^{12} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$); the comparison between the phonon-mediated attraction and the finite pairing threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the two-electron Cooper problem and relies on approximations such as the quasiboson approximation and neglecting retardation effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single-particle bands, the particle-hole excitation spectrum showing collective modes (phonon, plasmon), and the real-space pair density, confirming the chiral p-wave nature.
paper_structure: The paper builds from initial observations in graphene to constructing an effective fermion-boson Hamiltonian, solving the two-electron problem using approximations, and finally determining the superconducting pairing symmetry.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the methodology of using collective excitations (bosons) to mediate pairing in a strongly correlated, non-equilibrium system shares conceptual links with how bosonic mediators are treated in some AMO contexts, though the physical system is distinct.
